players.product: Susquehanna nuclear + PJM baseload gas generation contracted to data centers (Amazon ~2 GW PPA, powered-land sites)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $1.035 billion and adjusted free cash flow of $524 million, exceeding the high end of the revised guidance ranges mainly because Freedom and Guernsey closed in November 2025; Q4 alone delivered adjusted EBITDA of $382 million and adjusted free cash flow of $292 million ('higher than all of 2024'). Drivers: higher capacity prices and RMR revenues from June 2025, 'the continued ramp of AWS revenues', 5 weeks of Freedom and Guernsey, higher power prices net of hedges; offset by the Susquehanna Unit 2 extended outage and no PTC in 2025. Fleet generated approximately 40 terawatt hours, about 10% more than in 2024, with a 4.7% equivalent forced outage factor.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 adj EBITDA $1.035 billion; adj FCF $524 million; Q4 $382 million / $292 million; approximately 40 terawatt hours (about 10% more than in 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: Reaffirmed 2026 guidance, which excludes the pending Cornerstone acquisition (close anticipated this summer): adjusted EBITDA $1.75 billion to $2.05 billion and adjusted free cash flow $980 million to $1.18 billion; 2026 FCF per share forecast 'more than double' 2025. Cornerstone expected to add more than $4 of annual adjusted FCF per share upon closing; asked whether an analyst's $500 million EBITDA figure is a fair 12-month run rate for Cornerstone, the CFO said 'that's a good run rate number'. Liquidity more than $2 billion ($1.2 billion of cash plus the undrawn $900 million revolver); net leverage 3.0x as of February 20 on 2026 guidance midpoint, target below 3.5x by year-end 2026 after Cornerstone.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 adj EBITDA $1.75 billion to $2.05 billion; adj FCF $980 million to $1.18 billion; Cornerstone more than $4 FCF/share; net leverage 3.0x

quarterly_data.signal: Demand backdrop cited by management: largest hyperscalers' capex forecasts show 'over $650 billion of estimated spend' in 2026; latest PJM forecast has PPL zone peak load rising over 70% in the next 5 years and AEP zone over 30%; AEP reported 4 gigawatts of contracted PJM load growth in 2026 with approximately 90% of its 15 gigawatts of incremental load through 2030 backed by take-or-pay ESAs; PPL expects 10 gigawatts of signed agreements by end of Q1 2026. CFO: Talen's roughly 2 gigawatts of announced PPA is '2 of the 10' in the PPL zone; ESAs are 'a good kind of leading indicator of PPAs coming'. CEO: contract discussions across the fleet and pipeline 'have not slowed down'.
quarterly_data.figure: over $650 billion hyperscaler capex (2026); PPL zone peak load over 70% / AEP over 30% (5 years); PPL 10 gigawatts of signed agreements (by end of Q1 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: PJM market tightness: CEO says the last capacity auction 'would have cleared over $500 if it had not been for the $330 cap'; PJM, with governors' support, intends to extend the price collar for 2 more base residual auctions. PJM spark spreads for 2026-2028 rose over 15% from end of July to year-end, letting the commercial team layer in additional 2026 and 2027 hedges; hedging stays 'pragmatic, not programmatic' against stated targets of 60 to 80 (prompt) and 40 to 60 (prompt plus 1), running at the lower end, with the book heading toward being 'long 10,000 megawatts' in 2027 after Freedom, Guernsey and Cornerstone.
quarterly_data.figure: last auction would have cleared over $500 vs $330 cap; 2026-2028 spark spreads up over 15%

quarterly_data.signal: New build and the Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP, formerly RBA): Talen is working on new-build opportunities across batteries, CTs and CCGTs and will look to participate once rules are defined — 'with a 15-year contract at the right price, you can make the math work'. CEO: new build requires either an RBP award or an offtake contract, and 'it is the offtake agreement that defines this... not necessarily the turbine orders or the EPC'; a Chief Asset Development Officer role now focuses on technology, costing and EPC. CFO expects hybrid models: existing generation powering the first 3- to 5-year data center build-out in Pennsylvania, Ohio and Indiana, later backed by an upsized or second PPA for new generation. CEO: existing assets can still be contracted front-of-the-meter ('Yes').
quarterly_data.figure: 15-year contract (RBP) needed to finance new build

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline and Montour: after the Montour County commissioners' decision, the CEO said Talen will no longer discuss development publicly, while working 'numerous other organic and inorganic sites' across PJM (powered land and new build). The illustrative new 1 gigawatt data center PPA on Slide 11 is 'more than likely post-2028' because delivery would not start until '28 and then ramp, regardless of when it is signed in 2026; 'soon '29 will become the new '28' for data center power.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 gigawatt illustrative new data center PPA, delivery likely post-2028

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio growth and capital allocation: Freedom and Guernsey added approximately 2.8 gigawatts of efficient CCGTs (closed late November), greater than 40% accretive to FCF per share; agreement to acquire 3 Cornerstone generation assets in Ohio and Indiana, where Western PJM has 'significant data center tailwinds'. Talen has bought back over $2 billion of stock (close to 24% of the float) at an average $149 a share over 2.5 years and expanded the repurchase program to $2 billion through 2028; capital is directed to buybacks, M&A or new build targeting 'high teens returns'.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 2.8 gigawatts CCGTs acquired; over $2 billion bought back (24% of float, $149 a share)

connects_to.relationship: long-term nuclear PPA — Susquehanna campus power supply to AWS data centers (~2 GW)

contracts.signal: The 'Amazon 2.0 PPA' executed in June 2025 moved the Susquehanna deal to a front-of-the-meter arrangement and upsized volumes to 1.9 gigawatts in total; Talen is obligated to deliver anywhere in Pennsylvania, so other Amazon data centers can take power early (the '480 acceleration' lever). By 2028 the contract reaches only the first 480 megawatts; Slide 11 shows the upside of accelerating to 960 (full contract 1920). Growing AWS contracted margin makes hedging 'a little bit more opportunistic'.
